All three numeric Event Object* pointers are body+8; field writes use the body. Prepared inherited autoStart member offset +0xc is evidenced by Event registration 0x100332290. Trigger cases execute original CreateTriggerEvent 0x10032ecf0, uint32 hinted insertion 0x1003320e0, insert balancing 0x1001a7bb0, nonempty recursive destruction 0x10032fa30, GetMaxTypeIdx 0x10032f1d0, OnLevelLoad 0x10032e540, Update 0x10032ea90, Dispatch 0x10032f5b0, both original sorters 0x100330980/0x1003315d0 and Enable/SetEnabled/Start 0x10032e2f0/0x10032e2c0/0x10032ef60. All 31 real FloatAdd and all 4 real SetFloat configurations also execute original construction, trigger registration, original-order field load/reference remapping, OnLevelLoad and Update, with original enable/stop/re-enable requests. Compare loaded scalar fields, optional pointer fallbacks, aliased feedback, upper-before-lower clamping, one-shot same-frame finish, SetFloat load/reset/capture, variable GameTime scaling and progress completion. SetFloat logf/expf remain Linux libm service outputs captured as input/result bit pairs and replayed with input verification; original macOS libm and target-hardware math are not established. Compare every frame including the post-load state, Barn sequence counter, low Barn allocation, high load-heap baseline and complete registry/tree memory. Unique exhaustion, class-index limits, callback counter mutation/reload, uint8 wrapping, tree rotations/reuse and nonempty cleanup retain original failure side effects. Pool and scratch/load-heap boundaries remain explicit services; a vtable service queries the original max function by default and supplies boundary maxima/mutations for diagnostic cases. Reflection routes original constructor, allocation/registration and release bodies but uses a prepared single-slot release lookup. No complete TGCL/scene loading, game UI lifecycle or hardware parity is established.
